newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus market stabilises after declines-Laiki.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus market stabilises after declines-Laiki.

text.p: The Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) has stabilised following a slump in the past weeks and is starting to recover, Laiki Investments brokerage said in a weekly report.
The Laiki Investment index, set in 1993 at 100 points, closed on Monday at 182.97, registering marginal daily gains of 0.14 percent. The traditional resistence level of the bourse is 190.

"It is still not accompanied by high volume of transactions, a fact we have repeatedly noted gives a temporary character to the recent slump," Laiki Investments, which is a subsidiary of the Cyprus Popular Bank, said in a technical analysis.

The 10 day moving average of the market is moving downwards though is currently showing some signs of recovery. The 30 day moving average, the company said, is still on a downwards trend and does not seem strong enough to reverse the trend unless the recent upturn gathers pace.
"The medium term moving average is still clearly moving above the short term moving average, a fact which emphasises that we are still in a bearish market state," said Laiki Investments.
The 200 day long-term moving average is hovering around 191 points, it said.
